For OCONUS, transportation must also comply with regulations governing transportation from the point of the manufacturing plant to the place of final site placement at host country.
Standards must comply with permanent construction for off-site and modular construction.

children.content:
302.1.1 Existing Building Minimum Requirements [Addition]
Facilities, as they exist, must meet the requirements within the applicable occupancy chapter of NFPA 101.
Facilities that do not meet the requirements of NFPA 101 for existing occupancies must conform to one of the following:
a.
Upgrade the deficiency to meet the existing occupancy requirements, or
b.
Establish management protocols to provide a level of life safety equivalent to that required by NFPA 101 for existing occupancies, until an upgrade project can be completed.
Management protocols must be in writing and approved by the BO/AHJ.
302.2.2 Requirements for High Performance and Sustainable Building Features and Systems [Addition]
For existing buildings undergoing renovations, the systems and components included in the scope of the project must meet the requirements of UFC 1-200-02.
Refer to UFC 1-200-02 for project requirements.
302.2.3 Antiterrorism Upgrades for Inhabited Buildings [Addition]
Incorporate antiterrorism upgrades as required to bring entire existing inhabited buildings into compliance with UFC 4-010-01 for all building renovations, modifications, repairs, revitalizations, and restorations where project costs exceed 50% of the replacement cost of the existing building in accordance with UFS 3-701-01 except as stated otherwise in UFC 4-010-01.
The project costs used to compare against the 50% threshold are exclusive of the additional costs identified to meet these antiterrorism standards.
Where project costs do not exceed the 50% threshold, compliance with the antiterrorism standards is recommended, but not required.
Incorporate antiterrorism upgrades as required in UFC 4-010-01 whenever any building, or portion of a building, is converted from low occupancy to inhabited occupancy.
302.2.4 Requirements for New Fire Protection and Life Safety Systems [Addition]
Where the Building Rehabilitation chapter of NFPA 101 requires newly constructed elements, components, and systems to comply with new construction requirements in NFPA 101, then it must also comply with new construction requirements in UFC 3-600-01.
302.2.5 Fire Protection and Life Safety Upgrades [Addition]
Where project costs exceed 50 percent of the replacement cost of the existing building in accordance with UFS 3-701-01, then the entire building must be brought up to the fire protection and life safety system requirements for new construction in UFC 3-600-01.
Project costs to bring the building more into compliance with NFPA 101 do not count towards the 50 percent threshold.
302.2.6 NOT USED
302.2.7 Phased Projects [Addition]
Projects or programs involving floor plan reconfiguration that will encompass more than 50 percent of the area of a floor, or project or program costs exceeding 50 percent of the replacement cost of the existing building in accordance with UFS 3-701-01, that are planned in a phased approach or have separate projects to improve various parts of the facility must conform to the requirements for new construction.
These requirements are not applicable if the time from the start of design of the first phase to the start of design of the phase involving floor plan reconfiguration that exceeds 50 percent of the area, or project cost exceeds 50 percent of the replacement cost of the existing building in accordance with UFS 3-701-01, is greater than five years.
302.2.8 Low Impact Development Requirements [Addition]
For projects in the United States, United States Territories and Possessions of the United States involving the expansion of one or more buildings as part of its primary scope (i.e., primary facilities versus supporting facilities) with a “footprint” greater than 5,000 gross square feet (464.5 square meters), incorporate the low impact development (LID) requirements in UFC 3-210-10.
“Footprint” does not include existing building area to be renovated or existing impervious surfaces.
For Navy only: Use FC 1-300-09N for renovation projects exceeding $5 million with a stormwater component.

commentary.content: The intent of upgrading fire alarm and mass notification devices throughout the remainder of the building is to provide a uniform notification strategy. For example, a facility has existing clear and amber strobes throughout with no textual signs. The new requirement may be only clear strobes with textual signs. The floor being brought up to UFC 3-600-01 new construction requirements, and means of egress serving this floor, will require clear strobes and textual signs installed per the new criteria. The remainder of the floors will be modified so there are only clear strobes and textual signs, and the work must not make these other floors less conforming to UFC 3-600-01 requirements.

children.content: 10 U.S. Code § 2228 establishes the Office of Corrosion Policy and Oversight (OCPO) within the DoD, mandating a comprehensive strategy for preventing and mitigating corrosion on all military equipment and infrastructure.   The office is overseen by the Director, OCPO, ensuring defense assets maintain readiness and life expectancy through lifecycle management, and requiring annual reports to Congress on funding and return on investment.   Corrosion is defined in 10 USC §2228(f) (1) as, “The deterioration of a material or its properties due to a reaction of that material with its chemical environment.”

The office is overseen by the Director, OCPO, ensuring defense assets maintain readiness and life expectancy through lifecycle management, and requiring annual reports to Congress on funding and return on investment.
Corrosion is defined in 10 USC §2228(f) (1) as, “The deterioration of a material or its properties due to a reaction of that material with its chemical environment.”

commentary.content: Traditionally, corrosion has been thought of only as deterioration of metal (for example, rusting of steel); however, some non-traditional examples include rotting of wood, degradation of concrete (for example, carbonation and alkali-silica reaction phenomena), and degradation of composite materials due to reaction with the environment.

children.content: Projects in benign environments must consider the most stringent options stated in UFCs and UFGS for corrosion mitigation whenever possible, considering life-cycle maintenance costs and potential for corrosive microenvironments (e.g., sulfur compounds, carbon dioxide, chlorides, soot, fly ash, other industrial emissions).

children.content: Projects in corrosion prone locations are required to apply the most stringent options for corrosion mitigation identified in any UFC and/or UFGS.   If a location meets any of the following criteria, the location is considered a corrosion prone location.  Subsequent paragraphs provide criteria for the DOR to identify indoor and outdoor environmental severity category (ESC), climate zone (CZ) and immersion service category (Im) in order to make this determination. Exterior exposed metallic elements at a location with an ESC of C3, C4, or C5.   Includes areas open to the exterior (for example, mechanical rooms and hangars), and spaces that are not conditioned by design or may not be conditioned during prolonged periods due to deployment or occupancy. Exterior exposed nonmetallic elements at a location with an ESC of C4 or C5. Locations where micro-environmental factors (e.g., prevailing winds, ventilation, waterfront environments, industrial emissions, soot, fly ash, sulfur compounds, carbon dioxide, chlorides, de-icing salt application, possible chemical splash/spillage, adverse weather events such as flooding or wind-driven rain, and penetrations of the building envelope) create a locally corrosive environment regardless of ESC.  Humid locations identified in ANSI/ASHRAE 169 as CZ 0A, 1A, 2A, 3A, 3C, 4C, and 5C.   High humidity interior areas (for example, bathrooms, locker rooms, laundry rooms, pools, natatoriums, and aquatic training facilities). Any project that falls under the Immersion service category (Im).
